title: God's principles of health
summary: The body is a gift from God and a temple of the Spirit. We approach health holistically: nutrition, exercise, rest, water, sunlight, temperance, and trust in God, along with our emotions, forgiveness, gratitude, joy, and service. The "Blue Zones" (including Loma Linda) show that God's principles for living truly serve a long life.

sections.heading: The body as a gift and a temple

items.comment: The body is a "temple of the Holy Spirit" - not my private property, but a gift in which God dwells. Caring for it is an act of worship, not a worship of the body.

questions.text: What changes in how you care for your health when you think of the body as a "temple" and not just your own property?

items.label: the "temple" of the body (naos)
items.content: In 1 Cor 6:19 Paul uses *naos* - not the whole temple complex, but the inner sanctuary, the place of God's real presence. The believer's body is therefore presented as the dwelling place of the Spirit, which gives the care of one's health a spiritual dimension, not a cosmetic one.

questions.text: How does understanding the body as *naos* (the sanctuary of the Spirit) change your motivation to care for your health?

items.label: "you are not your own"
items.content: Twice in the same letter (1 Cor 3:16-17 and 6:19-20) Paul calls believers God's temple, and the key sentence is: "you are not your own, you were bought with a price." The body belongs to God doubly - through creation and through redemption - and so caring for it is a moral matter, not merely hygiene or aesthetics.

questions.text: What changes in your daily choices when you are aware that the body is God's "through creation and through redemption"?

items.comment: "Whether you eat or drink... do everything for the glory of God." Everyday choices - including those at the table - can be a way of worshiping God.

questions.text: How can ordinary eating and drinking become a way of giving glory to God?

items.label: the principle of "God's glory" as life's goal
items.content: 1 Cor 10:31 expresses the "principle of God's glory": all of life - words, deeds, and thoughts - has one supreme goal. Choices about food and drink are therefore neither neutral nor trivial; they can either honor God or harm a person made in His image. This is a healthy compass, not the burden of legalism.

questions.text: How does the motto "everything for the glory of God" guard against two extremes: indifference and excessive fussiness?

items.comment: The apostle wishes that the recipient "may prosper and be in good health, just as his soul prospers." God desires the health of the whole person - body and inner life together.

questions.text: What does it tell us about God that He cares about the health of both body and soul?

items.label: health as shalom (wholeness)
items.content: The Hebrew *shalom* - one of the key words of the Bible - means far more than "peace": it is wholeness, fullness, harmony embracing body, emotions, spirit, and relationships. That is why biblical health is not merely the absence of disease, but the integrated well-being of the whole person living in harmony with God. This is the biblical foundation of the holistic view of health.

questions.text: How does caring for your health change when the goal is *shalom* (the wholeness of the whole person) and not just a fit body?

sections.heading: Holistic health: God's principles for living

items.comment: The original diet in Eden was based on plants, grains, and fruit. From the very beginning God cares about what a person eats - it is part of His good plan.

questions.text: What follows from the fact that God Himself provided for human food already in paradise?

items.label: diet as the one detailed health topic
items.content: Interestingly, the Bible does not offer a systematic "health manual," yet diet is one of the few areas it treats in some detail - already from Gen 1:29. Eden remains the pattern: plant-based food, exercise, rest, clean air, and sunlight. This is not a command under threat, but the restoring of what is good from the Creator's original plan.

questions.text: Which elements of the "Eden lifestyle" are easiest, and which hardest, to restore in your daily life?

items.comment: God's rhythm is work and rest - six days of work and a day of rest. Regular rest is not laziness, but a law of health written into creation.

questions.text: How does the rhythm of work and rest affect the health of your body and mind?

items.comment: Whoever strives for the goal "exercises self-control in all things" - temperance. Christian freedom is not the absence of limits, but mastery over oneself.

questions.text: Where today is "self-control" hardest for you, and where would it help the most?

items.label: enkrateia: self-control as a fruit of the Spirit
items.content: The Greek *enkrateia* ("self-control," "temperance") is at once the athlete's virtue in 1 Cor 9:25 and a fruit of the Spirit in Gal 5:23. Temperance has two sides: abstaining from what harms, and using moderately what is good. It is not a merit or asceticism for its own sake, but the Spirit's work that orders our desires.

questions.text: Where do you need *enkrateia* more today: in abstaining from something, or in moderation toward good things?

items.label: Daniel's test (Dan 1:8-16)
items.content: At the court of Babylon, Daniel and his companions "resolved in their hearts" to remain faithful to God's principles, and asked for a simple plant-based diet instead of the king's rich cuisine. The Bible links their choice with greater clarity of mind and better health. It is an example of temperance as an expression of faithfulness to God in a foreign environment, not a cult of health or a display of willpower.

questions.text: What does it mean for you today to "resolve in your heart" in the area of lifestyle, when those around you pull in a different direction?

items.comment: "A cheerful heart does good like medicine, but a downcast spirit dries up the bones." The Bible long ago linked the state of the spirit with the health of the body.

questions.text: How do your emotions and attitude show up in your body and strength?

items.label: mind and body: the unity of the person
items.content: The Hebrew proverb about a "cheerful heart" assumes something the Bible repeats everywhere: a person is a unity, not a patchwork of separate parts called "soul" and "body." The state of the mind really affects the body, and vice versa. That is why Paul prays that God would sanctify believers "completely: spirit, soul, and body" (1 Thess 5:23) - not three competing layers, but one person being made holy.

questions.text: Where have you recently seen in yourself that the state of your spirit showed up in your body - or the state of your body in your spirit?

items.comment: The fear of God and turning away from evil are "health for the body and refreshment for the bones." Living by God's wisdom truly serves the body.

questions.text: Where in your life can you see that spiritual choices translate into physical well-being?

sections.heading: The inner life that heals: gratitude, forgiveness, joy

items.comment: "Rejoice always... give thanks in everything." Gratitude and joy are not only spirituality - they are habits that heal the inner life.

questions.text: What specifically could you give thanks for today, even if not everything is going your way?

items.comment: God calls us to put away bitterness and anger, and to forgive "as God has forgiven us." An unforgiven wrong poisons not only relationships, but also the body.

questions.text: What burden are you carrying that forgiveness could free you from - physically as well?

items.comment: Jesus teaches us not to worry - because by worrying "no one can add an hour to his life." Trust in God removes the stress that truly wears down our health.

questions.text: How could trust in God lower your level of fear and tension day to day?

items.comment: "It is more blessed to give than to receive." Serving others, as research also shows, fosters a long and meaningful life.

questions.text: Whom could you serve today - and what do you think it would also change in you?

sections.heading: Blue Zones: when God's principles meet life

items.comment: God sets before us "life and death" and calls: "choose life." Holding fast to God is directly linked here with long life - not magically, but as the fruit of wise choices.

questions.text: What does "choosing life" practically mean for you in everyday decisions?

items.comment: God reveals Himself as "the one who heals." God's principles for living are not arbitrary prohibitions - they flow from the care of a Physician for our good.

questions.text: How does your attitude toward God's guidance change when you see in it the prescription of a Physician rather than prohibitions?

items.label: God "your physician" (rapha)
items.content: In Exod 15:26 God says of Himself literally: "I, the LORD, am your physician." The Hebrew verb *rapha* means "to heal, mend, restore" - and in the Bible it covers not only the body, but also relationships, the inner life, and reconciliation with God. God's principles of health therefore flow from the care of the Healer, and healing itself remains ultimately His gift, not our merit.

questions.text: What changes in how you receive God's guidance when it comes from "your Physician" rather than from a stern lawgiver?

items.comment: Bodily exercise "is of some value," but godliness is profitable "for the present life and the life to come." Bodily health is good - but the most lasting fruit comes from a life with God.

questions.text: How can you keep the balance: caring for the body without making it an idol?

items.label: the "Blue Zones" and Loma Linda
items.content: "Blue Zones" is a term popularized by research into regions with an above-average number of centenarians (including Okinawa, Sardinia, Ikaria, and Nicoya). One of them is the community of Loma Linda in California, which is largely religious, with a healthy lifestyle; observations link longevity with, among other things, a plant-based diet, regular rest, temperance, community support, and a life of faith. These are observational data (correlations) that illustrate rather than "prove" - reviewers should take care with cautious wording. As a healthy family note: the Bible also roots a person's health in healthy relationships. Gen 2:24 presents marriage as a lasting "one flesh," established at creation. Eph 5:21-6:4 describes a family built on mutual submission "in the fear of Christ," the husband's sacrificial love, respect, and raising children "in the discipline and instruction of the Lord" - without provoking them to anger. Ps 127-128 portrays children as a gift and a blessing of a home in which God is honored. A healthy, secure family relationship is one of the pillars of a long and full life.

questions.text: Which of these (mutual submission, sacrificial love, raising children without provoking them) would most strengthen your family?

application.text: God does not divide a person into "spiritual" and "physical." Your body is a gift and a temple of the Spirit, and God's principles for living - nutrition, exercise, rest, water, sunlight, temperance, trust - are not prohibitions, but the prescription of a Physician who loves you. To this is added the inner life: gratitude, forgiveness, joy, and serving others truly lengthen and enrich life, as the observations of the "Blue Zones" confirm. Yet the deepest pillar of health is trust in God and healthy relationships - especially in the family.
application.challenge: Choose one area of God's prescription for health this week (for example, more water and exercise, regular rest, an act of forgiveness, or a daily moment of gratitude) and intentionally make it a gift to God in your "temple." Write down what changed after seven days.
